_tuning_notes: Swamp/mangrove hippo: darker hue, a notch smaller (size_scale is the Phase 2 alias for scale), slightly tighter territory. Same entity class as river — registry proves itself again. Phase 3: breed_item melon (also the cage bait); cage_tier 2. RARITY: tier 'uncommon' supplies the spawn weight; group_size and nearby_cap are pinned here (2-4, cap 6). nearby_cap denies natural spawns when that many of this animal are already within 64 blocks — the fix for persistent CREATURE mobs accumulating forever. ECOLOGY 0.4.2: was the raw ids minecraft:swamp + mangrove_swamp, which silently excluded every Terralith swamp. #c:is_swamp carries both vanilla swamps (Fabric API) and Terralith's. BABY SIZE 0.4.2: baby_scale moved 0.5 -> 1.0. The client already bakes the baby mesh through vanilla's BabyModelTransform (body halved, head full size) and vanilla age scaling halves the hitbox, so a 0.5 here was a SECOND shrink and calves rendered at a quarter of adult size. 1.0 = vanilla baby proportions. TERRALITH PASS: excludes Terralith's ice_marsh — a frozen swamp is no more a hippo biome than a frozen river. SIZE PASS 0.4.6: scale set against MEASURED vanilla hitboxes rather than by eye (cow 0.90x1.40, horse 1.40x1.60, polar bear 1.40x1.40, ravager 1.95x2.20, wolf 0.60x0.85, turtle 1.20x0.40, ocelot 0.60x0.70, chicken 0.40x0.70). Attributes.SCALE is uniform and multiplies the MODEL and the HITBOX together, so this is the one lever that cannot desync them. a notch under the river hippo, as before; still 1.43x horse width. SIZE PASS revised: the first attempt scaled an already-wrong box. Measuring the baked meshes showed the hitboxes never matched the models — the hippo mesh was 1.06 blocks tall inside a 1.60 box (66% fill, a third of it empty air), while the gorilla mesh was LARGER than its hitbox (121%). Builder dimensions in MenagerieEntities now match the measured mesh, and this scale multiplies model and hitbox together from there, so the drawn animal fills the box it is struck in.
